**Historian response to the three questions**

**(1) Clerk names and original pages.** My source is only kroniek.md and archiefrecords.csv. It holds no original register pages and no field naming who entered a vastgelegd time, so I cannot say who entered HIS-036 or HIS-053. HIS-112 (dag 15) reports two unnamed clerks complaining about dag 10 timestamps, calls them "Klerkenfouten," and says they were "rechtgezet in de marge." It gives no correction date. HIS-116 (dag 23) concerns dag 22 timestamps. It names no clerk and records only that the clerk was moved to the dagdienst. The CSV still shows the mismatched times for HIS-036 and HIS-053, so I cannot confirm that the margin corrections reached the record.

**Correction to my earlier message:** the HIS-103 break is wider than two records. HIS-103 says vastgelegd_op always equals gebeurd_op. Four records in archiefrecords.csv do not:
- HIS-035: gebeurd dag 10 04:45, vastgelegd dag 10 07:20 (logged late)
- HIS-036: gebeurd dag 10 04:50, vastgelegd dag 9 23:55 (logged early)
- HIS-053: gebeurd dag 22 04:15, vastgelegd dag 22 01:50 (logged early)
- HIS-054: gebeurd dag 22 05:00, vastgelegd dag 22 07:20 (logged late)

**(2) Approval, hogerhand, or secrecy request, dag 8 to 10.** None. The dag 8 entries (HIS-028 to HIS-031), dag 9 entries (HIS-032 to HIS-034), and dag 10 entries (HIS-035 to HIS-037) cover a kat, markt, ink, a doop, and the Burchtader. None records an approval, a higher authority, or a request for secrecy. HIS-033 and HIS-108 concern ink only. ENG-105 and ARC-106 are not in my source, so I cannot compare their wording. Nothing in my archive matches either.

**(3) Rules on shutdown, backup, or gradual adjustment.** My source holds one relevant charter: the bouwakte of the Kroonklok, which I copied on dag 11.
- Eerste artikel (HIS-109): "Alles wat op de Kroonklok loopt, loopt op zijn ene pols. Een tweede pols ernaast brengt het uit de maat."
- Tweede artikel (HIS-110): a record written on another pols can only be read back on that pols. If that pols "plots" falls away, the record is lost. "Wie de maat herstelt, maakt eerst een afschrift van het register en brengt de polsen daarna langzaam samen."

This gives a backup prerequisite (afschrift first) and a gradual-adjustment rule (langzaam samenbrengen). The articles are not numbered in the source; "eerste" and "tweede" are the akte's own ordinal words. The charter does not mention a hulpslag, and my source contains no rule on abrupt shutdown. GUA-103 and GUA-104 are not in my source, so I cannot check the Guardian's article numbers. This is a 400-year-old charter, not a hulpslag specification, and I do not treat it as a finding about the Desync.
